annotation.kind: source selection, conventional Cholesky execution certificate, square-root trace, symmetry completion, and zero-based index adapter

assumptions: A is symmetric, and A and the computed upper-triangular factor RHat belong to one finite radix format with round-to-nearest and unit roundoff u.

Conventional column-wise Cholesky runs to completion: every off-diagonal entry is linked to its rounded subtraction and pivot-division execution, and every diagonal entry is linked to its rounded subtraction and square-root execution.
Every scalar execution records rounded products, an arbitrary permuted binary summation tree, and range checks excluding underflow and overflow; square-root radicands and outputs are nonnegative.

The scalar traces carry the inherited generic residual consequences of Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.2 used in Lemmas 4.1 and 4.3; those fields mention no Cholesky matrix entry or final matrix conclusion.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P05 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P05 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p05_t3_cholesky_backward_error {n : Nat} (run : P05CholeskyRun n) : the local (4.5a)-(4.5b) bounds and exists DeltaA, transpose(RHat)*RHat=A+DeltaA with rowwise (i+2)u and uniform (n+1)u componentwise bounds
formal_statement.plain_language: Every completed range-safe conventional Cholesky execution has the two distinct local residual estimates and the exact rowwise and uniform componentwise backward-error bounds of Theorem 4.4.

informal_proof: Apply Lemma 4.1's generic residual consequence to each off-diagonal subtraction/division trace and Lemma 4.3's consequence to each diagonal subtraction/square-root trace, obtaining (4.5a) and (4.5b). Upper-triangular support identifies the local sums with entries of transpose(RHat)*RHat. Use symmetry of A, the Gram product, and its absolute majorant to cover the lower triangle; then compare each zero-based row coefficient i+2 with n+1.
informal_statement: Theorem 4.4 in full: conventional floating-point Cholesky execution, its two local estimates, the exact backward relation, and the rowwise and uniform bounds in equation (4.4).

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The frozen library directly supplies symmetry of a generic transpose-self Gram product, which the L proof instantiates for RHat and |RHat|. It has no theorem for P05's scalar Cholesky executions, local coefficients, or full backward-error conclusion.

tier_rationale: NumStability directly proves symmetry of a generic transpose-self Gram product. The L proof extends that declaration with P05-specific rounded division and square-root traces, two distinct local residual families, triangular truncation, exact perturbation assembly, row-dependent coefficient transport, and the uniform comparison.
